```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "-")
library(dplyr)

source(file = here::here("R", "vegetation", "config.R"))
paths <- veg_config$paths

# Every number in this report is read from the CSV files written by
# R/vegetation/01 to 03 (data/processed/ and outputs/vegetation/). Nothing is
# typed by hand.
read_out <- function(path) readr::read_csv(file = path, show_col_types = FALSE)

survey_all <- read_out(path = paths$survey_summary)
survey_sens <- read_out(path = paths$survey_summary_sens)
plot_all <- read_out(path = paths$plot_summary)
plot_sens <- read_out(path = paths$plot_summary_sens)
totals <- read_out(path = paths$totals)
exclusions <- read_out(path = paths$exclusions)
flags <- read_out(path = paths$flags)
catalogue <- read_out(path = paths$catalogue)
records <- read_out(path = paths$record_taxa)

tot_all <- filter(.data = totals, version == "accepted")
tot_sens <- filter(.data = totals, version == "excluding_errors")
shift <- veg_plot_shift(plot_all = plot_all, plot_sens = plot_sens)

# Formatting helpers
f1 <- function(x) if_else(condition = is.na(x), true = NA_character_, false = sprintf(fmt = "%.1f", x))
f2 <- function(x) if_else(condition = is.na(x), true = NA_character_, false = sprintf(fmt = "%.2f", x))
pct0 <- function(x) sprintf(fmt = "%.0f%%", 100 * x)
short <- function(x) sub(pattern = "^SavMon_LW_", replacement = "", x = x)
table_md <- function(data, align) knitr::kable(x = data, format = "pipe", align = align)

# Counts used in the prose
surveyed <- filter(.data = plot_all, surveyed)
not_surveyed <- filter(.data = plot_all, !surveyed)
n_flags_severity <- function(what) sum(flags$severity == what)
n_checks_fired <- n_distinct(flags$check_id)
n_named_placeholder <- sum(grepl(pattern = "^(herb|wood)_[0-9]+ [(]", x = records$species_name))
n_unknown_records <- sum(records$taxon_class != "identified")
n_additional <- sum(records$source == "additional_repeat")
n_submissions <- nrow(survey_all)
n_rejected <- sum(survey_all$review_state == "rejected", na.rm = TRUE)
n_sensitivity_changed <- sum(shift$gamma_richness_change != 0)
backup <- filter(.data = plot_all, plot_status == "backup")
named_labels <- records$species_name[grepl(pattern = "^(herb|wood)_[0-9]+ [(]", x = records$species_name)] |>
  sub(pattern = " .*", replacement = "") |>
  unique()
n_named_labels <- length(named_labels)
n_named_also_bare <- sum(is.element(el = named_labels, set = records$unknown_label))
effort <- read_out(path = paths$effort)
effort_sens <- read_out(path = paths$effort_sens)
n_eff <- nrow(effort)
n_full <- sum(effort$n_quadrats >= veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot)
n_asym <- sum(effort$approaches_asymptote)
asym_plots <- short(x = effort$plot_name[effort$approaches_asymptote])
n_asym_sens <- sum(effort_sens$approaches_asymptote)
n_not_asym <- n_eff - n_asym
n_est_ok <- sum(effort$estimate_status == "ok")
n_sens_short <- sum(effort_sens$n_quadrats < veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot)
n_comp_low <- sum(effort$completeness < 0.5)
n_cov_low <- sum(effort$sample_coverage < veg_config$coverage_min)
rank_cor <- cor(x = shift$gamma_richness_all, y = shift$gamma_richness_sens, method = "spearman")
```

## 1. TL;DR

- **What.** A summary of the herbaceous vegetation survey by submission
  (`r n_submissions` submissions, `r n_rejected` of them rejected in ODK) and by plot
  (`r tot_all$n_plots_surveyed` of `r tot_all$n_plots_registered` registered plots surveyed,
  `r tot_all$n_surveys` accepted surveys, `r tot_all$n_quadrats` quadrats), and a map of the
  transects. Data are only counted and flagged, never changed. Sampling effort
  (brief item 1c) is assessed in section 5.
- **Key result.** Only `r n_asym` of `r n_eff` plots approach an asymptote: 20 quadrats do not
  saturate the species curve for the other `r n_not_asym` (section 5). Plots hold `r tot_all$gamma_richness_min` to `r tot_all$gamma_richness_max`
  identified taxa (median `r tot_all$gamma_richness_median`;
  `r tot_all$richness_all_plots` taxa in the whole data set). Richness is what 20 quadrats
  found, so it is a minimum, and completeness differs between plots, so comparisons should account for it.
- **Key decision.** Richness counts identified taxa only. Provisional unknowns
  (`herb_NNN` labels) are kept apart: they add `r tot_all$n_unknown_labels_all_plots` labels and
  are in `r pct0(tot_all$share_quadrats_unknown)` of the quadrats. Leaving out the records with an
  error flag gives `r tot_sens$richness_all_plots` taxa in the data set
  (against `r tot_all$richness_all_plots`) and changes the gamma richness of `r n_sensitivity_changed` plots.
- **What remains uncertain, and what Tech must do.** Many unknowns are probably named taxa (section 8.4).
  The data cannot tell abundance, only presence in a quadrat. Tech must stop the form from
  accepting free-text names that do not follow `Genus_species`, and must give each `herb_NNN`
  label a name in the entity list once it is identified, so that the same plant is counted once.

## 2. Data and checks overview

The report reads the tables staged by `R/vegetation/01_load_join.R` (`r n_submissions` survey
submissions, `r sum(survey_all$n_quadrats)` quadrats, `r nrow(records)` species records, of which
`r sum(records$source == "selected_list")` picked from the species list and
`r n_additional` typed or reused in the extra-species repeat) and the flags written by
`R/vegetation/02_run_checks.R`. Of the `r n_submissions` submissions, `r n_rejected` were rejected in
ODK: they are listed in the survey table and kept in the flags, but are not counted in the plot or
headline numbers and are not on the list for the field teams.

### 2.1 Flags

The catalogue has `r nrow(catalogue)` checks; `r n_checks_fired` of them raised at least one
flag. Errors break a rule of the survey protocol or contradict other answers; warnings need a
look; info is context.

```{r flag-counts}
flags |>
  count(severity, level) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = n, values_fill = 0L) |>
  mutate(total = rowSums(across(.cols = where(is.numeric)))) |>
  arrange(match(x = severity, table = veg_severities)) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

There are `r n_flags_severity(what = "error")` errors, `r n_flags_severity(what = "warning")`
warnings and `r n_flags_severity(what = "info")` info flags. The errors and warnings, with the
person who can resolve each, are in `issues_for_field_teams.md`; the full list is
`outputs/vegetation/flags.csv`.

### 2.2 How flags enter the summaries

Each survey and plot row shows the number of flags of each severity (columns E, W, I), counted on
the whole submission. Flags never remove a record from the main tables. The plot rows and the
headline numbers count the submissions that were not rejected in ODK, and the flag counts in a plot
row come from those submissions; the survey rows show every submission, rejected ones included.
Section 7 shows what changes when the error-flagged quadrats are left out.

## 3. Survey-level summary (brief item a)

One row per survey submission (one visit to one plot). A quadrat has "species" when at least one
species record exists for it, identified or not.

```{r survey-table}
survey_all |>
  mutate(
    plot = short(x = plot_name),
    status = review_state
  ) |>
  select(
    plot, date = survey_date, recorder, `duration (min)` = duration_min, n_quadrats,
    `with species` = n_quadrats_with_species, taxa = richness, unknowns = n_unknown_labels,
    E = n_error, W = n_warning, I = n_info, review = status
  ) |>
  mutate(review = coalesce(review, "")) |>
  arrange(plot, date) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"))
```

- `taxa` is the number of identified taxa in the submission (section 8.1).
- `unknowns` is the number of different provisional labels (`herb_NNN`), not counted in `taxa`.
- `duration (min)` is the time from the start to the end of the form.
- `review` is the ODK review state. It is empty when no state is recorded, which is the case for every
  submission except the rejected ones.

Across submissions, `taxa` runs from `r min(survey_all$richness)` to `r max(survey_all$richness)`
(median `r median(survey_all$richness)`). Durations run from `r f1(min(survey_all$duration_min))`
to `r f1(max(survey_all$duration_min))` minutes (median `r f1(median(survey_all$duration_min))`).
Every submission has `r unique(survey_all$n_quadrats)` quadrats.
`r sum(survey_all$n_quadrats_with_species < survey_all$n_quadrats)` submissions have at least one
quadrat without any species record.
`r sum(survey_all$review_state == "rejected", na.rm = TRUE)` submissions are rejected in ODK; each belongs to
a plot that also has an accepted submission. They are listed here but not counted in the
plot rows or the headline numbers.

## 4. Plot-level summary (brief item b)

One row per registered plot, from the submissions that were not rejected in ODK. Two plots
(`r paste(short(x = filter(.data = survey_all, review_state == "rejected")$plot_name), collapse = " and ")`)
were submitted twice and one of the two submissions was rejected, so only the accepted one counts: no
plot has more than `r max(plot_all$n_quadrats)` quadrats.

```{r plot-table}
plot_all |>
  mutate(
    plot = short(x = plot_name),
    `taxa (gamma)` = gamma_richness,
    `mean per quadrat` = f2(mean_quadrat_richness),
    `unknown quadrats` = if_else(condition = surveyed, true = pct0(share_quadrats_unknown), false = NA_character_),
    state = if_else(condition = surveyed, true = "surveyed", false = "not surveyed")
  ) |>
  select(
    plot, type = plot_status, state, surveys = n_surveys, n_quadrats,
    `taxa (gamma)`, `mean per quadrat`, `unknown quadrats`,
    unknowns = n_unknown_labels, E = n_error, W = n_warning
  ) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "l", "l", rep(x = "r", times = 8)))
```

- `taxa (gamma)` is the number of identified taxa found in all the quadrats of the plot.
- `mean per quadrat` is the average number of identified taxa in one 1 m x 1 m quadrat. It does not
  depend on the number of quadrats, so it compares plots with different effort.
- `unknown quadrats` is the share of the plot's quadrats with at least one provisional unknown.
- `type` is the plot status in the registration: primary or backup.

`r nrow(surveyed)` of the `r nrow(plot_all)` registered plots were surveyed. The plot not surveyed is
`r paste(short(x = not_surveyed$plot_name), collapse = ", ")`
(`r paste(not_surveyed$plot_status, ifelse(test = not_surveyed$is_viable == "no", yes = "and not viable", no = "and viable"), collapse = "; ")`
in the registration). The backup plot `r paste(short(x = backup$plot_name), collapse = ", ")` was surveyed
and has `r backup$gamma_richness` taxa, against a median of
`r median(filter(.data = surveyed, plot_status == "primary")$gamma_richness)` for the surveyed primary plots.

## 5. Assessment of sampling effort (brief item c)

Is 20 quadrats enough to describe the plant community of a plot? The data hold presence or absence of a
taxon in each 1 m x 1 m quadrat, so the question is answered with incidence-based methods: the
quadrats are the sampling units, and only identified taxa are used (section 8.1). The assessment is
provisional: the thresholds below are working values to confirm with Natural State.

- `r n_eff` plots were surveyed; `r n_full` of them have the `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot`
  quadrats expected, so the effort is the same everywhere and differences are in what the quadrats found.
- Only `r n_asym` of `r n_eff` plots approach an asymptote (`r paste(asym_plots, collapse = " and ")`).
  For the other `r n_not_asym`, `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats do not saturate the
  species curve.
- Completeness (observed taxa divided by the Chao2 estimate) runs from `r pct0(min(effort$completeness))`
  to `r pct0(max(effort$completeness))` (median `r pct0(median(effort$completeness))`). Sample coverage runs
  from `r f2(min(effort$sample_coverage))` to `r f2(max(effort$sample_coverage))` (median
  `r f2(median(effort$sample_coverage))`).

### 5.1 Method

For each plot the `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats are the columns of a taxon-by-quadrat
presence matrix (`R/functions/veg_effort.R`, run by `R/vegetation/03_summaries.R`). Quadrats without any
identified taxon stay in the matrix, because an empty quadrat is information about effort.

- **Accumulation curve.** `vegan::specaccum(method = "random")` adds quadrats in random order
  (`r veg_config$accumulation_permutations` orderings, seed `r veg_config$seed` in the configuration) and
  the mean number of taxa is drawn against the number of quadrats. A curve that is still rising at the
  last quadrat says that more quadrats would still find new taxa.
- **Chao2 richness.** The `iNEXT` package estimates the asymptotic richness from the incidence data
  (`r n_est_ok` of `r n_eff` plots gave an estimate), with a 95% interval. It uses the taxa seen in one and in two
  quadrats only, so it is a lower bound of the true richness.
- **Completeness** is observed taxa divided by the Chao2 estimate.
- **Sample coverage** (`iNEXT`) is the share of the plot's taxa, weighted by how often they occur, that
  the sample has already found.
- **Gain over the last `r veg_config$accumulation_tail_quadrats` quadrats** is the number of taxa the
  mean curve adds between quadrat `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot - veg_config$accumulation_tail_quadrats`
  and quadrat `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot`. It is a plain reading of the slope of the curve.
- **Approaches an asymptote** when completeness is at least `r veg_config$completeness_min` and sample
  coverage is at least `r veg_config$coverage_min`. Both thresholds are provisional.

Two versions exist, as for the other tables. The main version uses the submissions that were not rejected
in ODK (`sampling_effort.csv`). The sensitivity version also leaves out the quadrats with an error flag
(`sampling_effort_excl_errors.csv`); `r n_sens_short` plot(s) then have fewer than
`r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats, which shows in the quadrat column of that file.

### 5.2 Results

```{r effort-table}
worst <- effort |>
  arrange(completeness) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(
    plot = short(x = plot_name),
    `Chao2 (95% interval)` = sprintf(fmt = "%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", estimated_richness, estimated_lcl, estimated_ucl),
    completeness = pct0(completeness),
    coverage = f2(sample_coverage),
    `approaches asymptote` = if_else(condition = approaches_asymptote, true = "yes", false = "no")
  ) |>
  select(plot, quadrats = n_quadrats, observed = observed_richness, `Chao2 (95% interval)`,
    completeness, coverage, `approaches asymptote`)
summary_row <- tibble(
  plot = "All plots (median; asymptote: count)",
  quadrats = as.character(median(effort$n_quadrats)),
  observed = as.character(median(effort$observed_richness)),
  `Chao2 (95% interval)` = sprintf(fmt = "%.1f", median(effort$estimated_richness)),
  completeness = pct0(median(effort$completeness)),
  coverage = f2(median(effort$sample_coverage)),
  `approaches asymptote` = paste(n_asym, "of", n_eff)
)
worst |>
  mutate(across(.cols = c(quadrats, observed), .fns = as.character)) |>
  bind_rows(summary_row) |>
  table_md(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"))
```

The ten plots with the lowest completeness are shown; all `r n_eff` plots are in
`outputs/vegetation/sampling_effort.csv`, with the gain over the last
`r veg_config$accumulation_tail_quadrats` quadrats (median `r f2(median(effort$gain_last_quadrats))` taxa,
range `r f2(min(effort$gain_last_quadrats))` to `r f2(max(effort$gain_last_quadrats))`). Per plot, the lowest
completeness is `r pct0(min(effort$completeness))` and `r n_comp_low` plots stay under 50%.
`r n_cov_low` of `r n_eff` plots have a coverage below `r veg_config$coverage_min`.

![Species accumulation curves of the surveyed plots: mean number of identified taxa (line) against the number of quadrats added in random order, one panel per plot. Description: most curves are still rising at the twentieth quadrat; a few flatten out near the end; plots differ widely in the height of the curve.](figures/veg_accumulation.png)

The Chao2 intervals are wide for the plots with many rare taxa (the upper limit exceeds three times the
observed richness in `r sum(effort$estimated_ucl > 3 * effort$observed_richness, na.rm = TRUE)` plots), so the
completeness of a single plot is uncertain; the pattern across plots is the robust part.
The sensitivity version gives `r n_asym_sens` plot(s) that approach an asymptote and a median completeness
of `r pct0(median(effort_sens$completeness))`, against `r pct0(median(effort$completeness))` in the main version.

### 5.3 What this means

- **The brief's question.** `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats do not saturate the species
  curve for `r n_not_asym` of `r n_eff` plots. More quadrats would still find new taxa there.
- **Plot comparisons.** The richness of a plot is a lower bound. Completeness varies a lot between plots
  (`r pct0(min(effort$completeness))` to `r pct0(max(effort$completeness))`), so a plot with fewer taxa may
  only be a plot that was sampled less completely. Plot richness comparisons should account for it,
  for example by comparing at equal coverage or by using the estimate with its interval, not the observed count alone.
- **For the data provider.** Adding quadrats in the plots with low completeness would improve their
  richness estimate. This is a statement about the adequacy of these data, not a recommendation on the
  survey design.

### 5.4 Decisions, alternatives and status

- **Incidence-based, quadrats as units.** Only presence or absence exists, so abundance-based estimators
  (Chao1, rarefaction on individuals) do not apply.
- **Chao2 and coverage together.** Alternative: the curves alone, which give no number and no rule for
  "enough". Alternative: Chao2 without coverage, which depends on one estimator that is unstable with few rare
  taxa. Both are reported, and the asymptote rule needs both.
- **Thresholds `r veg_config$completeness_min` and `r veg_config$coverage_min`.** Common working values
  for "near complete"; other values would change the count of `r n_asym` plots (a lower completeness
  threshold would add plots). They are provisional and to confirm with Natural State.
- **Identified taxa only.** Same rule as for richness (section 8.1): provisional unknowns are not stable units.
- **Random order, `r veg_config$accumulation_permutations` orderings.** The quadrats of a transect are
  spatially ordered, so the field order would mix spatial structure into the curve; random order gives the
  expected curve. The seed is fixed for reproducibility.
- **Status.** Provisional; the estimates and the thresholds are written in `rulebook.md`.

## 6. Map of transect locations (brief item d)

This section shows where the plots are and where the quadrats of a few plots were recorded, coloured by the
worst flag of the plot (or of the quadrat). Colour is the severity of the worst flag: error, then warning,
then info; a plot without a flag is green. The colours are defined once in the configuration and are
also used in the dashboard (section 6.3). Data are anonymised, so real coordinates are shown.

```{r map-setup}
locations <- read_out(path = paths$plot_locations)
spa04 <- filter(.data = flags, check_id == "SPA-04")
n_located <- sum(!is.na(locations$lon))
n_sev <- function(what) sum(locations$worst_severity == what & locations$surveyed)
not_drawn <- filter(.data = locations, is.na(lon) | is.na(lat))
backup <- filter(.data = locations, plot_status == "backup")
```

### 6.1 All plots

The overview places the `r n_located` registered plots that have coordinates in the plot register
(all `r sum(locations$surveyed)` surveyed plots; the plot centre is the geopoint stored as "latitude longitude altitude
accuracy" in the plot entity list). `r nrow(not_drawn)` registered plot
(`r paste(short(x = not_drawn$plot_name), collapse = ", ")`, not viable, not surveyed) has no coordinates and
cannot be drawn; it is named in the figure. The backup plot (`r short(x = backup$plot_name)`) is drawn as a
diamond. Distances use EPSG:32637 (UTM zone 37N), the zone used by the spatial checks. There is no web
basemap, so the figure works offline.

![Map of the plot locations. Circles are primary plots that were surveyed, the diamond is the backup plot. Fill is the worst flag of the plot: dark red error, amber warning, grey info only. A scale bar of 2 km and a north arrow are drawn. Description: 30 points in a band about 14 km wide from west to east and 5 km from south to north; three points lie to the north-east, away from the main band; most points are amber, with dark red points in the middle and the south-east and two grey points in the west.](figures/veg_transect_map.png)

What stands out:

- `r n_sev(what = "error")` surveyed plots have an error flag (dark red) and `r n_sev(what = "warning")` have
  at worst a warning. Only `r n_sev(what = "info")` plots (13 and 17) have no warning or error. No plot is free of flags,
  because every surveyed plot has info-level flags (mostly unknown taxa). Error plots are spread along the whole band, so
  the errors do not point to one area. They are data-entry errors (quadrats marked as having extra species
  with none recorded, one extra species without a name), not location problems.
- Four error plots (10, 14, 19, 30) lie in the south-east cluster, so a field team visiting that cluster can
  check four submissions in one trip.
- The backup plot `r short(x = backup$plot_name)` lies north-east next to plot 05 and about 5 km north of the
  main band; it has `r backup$n_error` error flags (the same kind of data-entry error).
- Plots 05, 09 and 46 are isolated to the north-east. They need their own trip, which matters for follow-up
  visits, not for data quality.

### 6.2 Quadrats along the transects

The second figure shows the quadrat fixes of four plots in metres from the plot centre, with the line joining
the quadrats in numbering order. The dashed circle has the radius of the belt reach (half the 50 m
length and half the 5 m width, `r round(veg_belt_reach_m(), 1)` m); the check SPA-04 flags a quadrat when it
lies beyond this reach plus the GPS accuracy of its fix and of the plot centre. The colour is the worst flag
of the quadrat (any check). Plots 01, 05 and 11 each have quadrats beyond the belt; plot 16 stays inside it.

![Quadrat positions of plots 01, 05, 11 and 16 in metres from the plot centre (cross), joined by a line in quadrat order. A dashed circle marks the reach of the belt; a 20 m scale bar and a north arrow are drawn. Description: in plot 01 one quadrat lies about 75 m to the north-west of the centre while the others cluster near the circle; in plot 05 a group of about eight quadrats lies north of the circle, outside the belt; in plot 11 one quadrat is about 50 m north; in plot 16 all quadrats sit along an east-west line inside the circle.](figures/veg_transect_zoom.png)

- Plot 01: one quadrat (18) is `r max(as.numeric(spa04$value[spa04$plot_name == "SavMon_LW_Plot_01"]))` m from the
  plot centre, far beyond the belt; the line to it shows one fix far from the others; the other 19 quadrats
  form a normal transect.
- Plot 05: the whole transect is shifted about 30 m north of the plot centre (`r sum(spa04$plot_name == "SavMon_LW_Plot_05")`
  quadrats flagged). Either the transect was laid out from another point or the plot centre is wrong; the
  data cannot tell which. This is the clearest case for a field team to check.
- Plot 11: one quadrat about 50 m away, like plot 01 (a single fix).
- Plot 16: a clean example, all fixes inside the belt.
- Overall `r nrow(spa04)` quadrats in `r n_distinct(spa04$plot_name)` plots are flagged by SPA-04 (warning). They
  are warnings, not errors, because the GPS may drift under tree cover and the plot centre is stored with
  3 to 5 m accuracy.

### 6.3 Interactive dashboard

An interactive version of these views is an extra, not part of the deliverable: the report stands alone.
The dashboard has four pages (summaries with survey and plot tables, a map of the plots coloured by
worst flag severity with a popup per plot, a flags table that can be filtered by severity, check and plot, and the sampling effort). It reads
the same files as this report (`outputs/vegetation/` and `figures/`) and runs no new analysis.

- Source: [`dashboard/`](dashboard/) (`dashboard.qmd`, Quarto `format: dashboard`); rendered page:
  `docs/index.html`.
- Planned address, once GitHub Pages is switched on:
  <https://albansagouis.github.io/naturalstate-take-home/>.
- The Natural State logo and colours are used for this mock-up only.

```{r dashboard-screenshots-check}
shots <- fs::path("figures", paste0("veg_dashboard_", c("summaries", "map", "flags"), ".png"))
stopifnot("dashboard screenshots are missing" = all(fs::file_exists(shots)))
```

## 7. Sensitivity: leaving out the records with an error flag

The plot and headline tables above exist a second time without the quadrats that carry an error
flag (`survey_summary_excl_errors.csv` and `plot_summary_excl_errors.csv`). Both versions leave out
the rejected submissions. What is left out is listed in `outputs/vegetation/excluded_records.csv`:

- the `r sum(exclusions$level == "quadrat" & exclusions$reason == "error_flag_quadrat")` quadrats that
  carry an error flag (only the quadrat, not the rest of the submission);
- the whole submission for an error that is not tied to a quadrat (none in these data);
- the `r nrow(filter(.data = exclusions, level == "survey", reason == "rejected_submission"))` submissions
  rejected in ODK, with their `r sum(exclusions$reason == "rejected_submission" & exclusions$level == "quadrat")`
  quadrats; they are left out of both versions, not only of this one.

```{r sensitivity-totals}
rows <- list(
  c("Surveys", tot_all$n_surveys, tot_sens$n_surveys),
  c("Quadrats", tot_all$n_quadrats, tot_sens$n_quadrats),
  c("Identified taxa, whole data set", tot_all$richness_all_plots, tot_sens$richness_all_plots),
  c("Provisional unknown labels", tot_all$n_unknown_labels_all_plots, tot_sens$n_unknown_labels_all_plots),
  c("Taxa upper bound (with unknown labels)", tot_all$richness_upper_bound_all_plots, tot_sens$richness_upper_bound_all_plots),
  c("Mean taxa per quadrat", f2(tot_all$mean_quadrat_richness), f2(tot_sens$mean_quadrat_richness)),
  c("Median taxa per plot (gamma)", tot_all$gamma_richness_median, tot_sens$gamma_richness_median),
  c("Maximum taxa per plot (gamma)", tot_all$gamma_richness_max, tot_sens$gamma_richness_max)
)
sens_table <- as.data.frame(do.call(what = rbind, args = rows))
names(sens_table) <- c("Number", "Accepted submissions", "Excluding errors")
table_md(data = sens_table, align = c("l", "r", "r"))
```

Per plot, the gamma richness changes in `r n_sensitivity_changed` of `r nrow(shift)` plots
(largest fall `r max(-shift$gamma_richness_change)` taxa, median change
`r median(shift$gamma_richness_change)`). The mean number of taxa per quadrat moves by at most
`r f2(max(abs(shift$mean_quadrat_richness_change)))`. The data-set richness is
`r ifelse(test = tot_all$richness_all_plots == tot_sens$richness_all_plots, yes = "unchanged", no = "lower")`
(a taxon only found in a left-out quadrat would lower it). The rank correlation of gamma richness
between the two versions is `r f2(rank_cor)`. The flag counts in the sensitivity tables are the same as in the main
tables (they describe the submissions); only quadrats, taxa and indices are recomputed.

## 8. Decisions and limits

### 8.1 What counts as a species

Distinct identified taxa are the names picked from the species list plus the names typed in
the extra-species repeat, after harmless typing differences are removed: outer and double
spaces are trimmed, spaces become underscores, the first letter is a capital. Each taxon is counted
once, however often it was recorded. A record such as `herb_104 (Justicia divaricata )` is read as its
proposed name, because the team named it (`r n_named_placeholder` records).

Provisional unknowns are the plain placeholders (`herb_017`), raw UUID text and records with no
name: `r n_unknown_records` of `r nrow(records)` records. They are counted separately and are
not in the headline richness, because the same plant can sit behind several labels and one label is
not a stable taxon. Including them would change the data-set richness from
`r tot_all$richness_all_plots` to `r tot_all$richness_upper_bound_all_plots`; the totals file
(`summary_totals.csv`) and the `richness_upper_bound` column of
`plot_summary.csv` give the same view. A misspelling (for example `Brachiara`) is not merged: it stays a
separate taxon and is flagged in the checks (SPE-06) for the field team.

### 8.2 Diversity indices

There is no abundance, only presence in each of the quadrats, so no abundance-based diversity
index exists, and a diversity index would say little about the vegetation. The tables therefore
report richness only (identified taxa, and with the provisional unknown labels added).
Shannon's H on quadrat frequencies (H = -sum(p ln p), with p the share of the plot's total
quadrat frequency) is used for one purpose: check PLT-09 flags a plot whose H is more than
`r veg_config$shannon_outlier_mad` scaled median absolute deviations from the median of the plots, as a
sign of an incomplete, repeated or misread species list. It needs at least
`r veg_config$shannon_outlier_min_plots` plots and raises an information flag for the data manager.
On the sample it flags `r sum(flags$check_id == "PLT-09")` plots. Alternatives: report H in the
plot table (rejected: invites reading it as a biodiversity result when twenty small quadrats
cannot support one), Simpson's index (the same objection), and no outlier check (rejected:
a plot with a single recorded taxon would pass unnoticed).

### 8.3 What the sensitivity version leaves out

A quadrat with an error flag is left out and the other quadrats of the submission stay: the errors
in these data are about one quadrat (extra species announced but not recorded; an extra species
without a name) and say nothing about the other 19. A submission rejected in ODK is left out of
both versions as a whole: the reviewer already judged it unusable, and counting it would give a plot
the quadrats of two visits. The data themselves are never changed: the tables are filtered views.
Warnings and info flags never exclude a record.

### 8.4 Limits

- Presence or absence only: no cover or counts, so no abundance-based diversity and no density.
- 20 quadrats per plot, 1 m x 1 m each, in one visit: richness is what those quadrats found, a
  minimum for the plot.
- The sampling-effort estimates (section 5) rest on `r veg_config$expected_quadrats_per_plot` quadrats per
  plot and provisional thresholds; Chao2 is a lower bound and its intervals are wide.
- `r n_unknown_records` records (`r pct0(n_unknown_records / nrow(records))`) are provisional unknowns, and the
  taxa behind them may be identified ones. If an unknown label were linked to a named taxon, richness
  would fall for plots where the same plant is counted twice and rise for plots whose unknowns are
  new taxa. Many of the `herb_NNN` labels with a proposed name also appear as a plain label in other
  quadrats (`r n_named_also_bare`
  of `r n_named_labels`),
  so a link table maintained by the data manager would remove most of the problem. It is not applied
  here because it would be a change to the data.
- Whether the reviewer was right to reject the two submissions is not checked: the report follows the
  ODK review state. The accepted and the rejected submission of a plot differ in duration, and in
  recorder for one plot, but the data do not say why one was rejected.
- A quadrat count per plot does not test whether the quadrats were placed as the protocol asks;
  the spatial checks are in the flag list.

## Reproduce

The numbers in this report come from the files in `data/processed/` and `outputs/vegetation/`. Script 05 renders the dashboard (it needs Quarto). To
regenerate and check them, run from the project root in a fresh R session:

```{r reproduce, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "01_load_join.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "02_run_checks.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "03_summaries.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "04_map.R"))
source(here::here("R", "vegetation", "05_dashboard.R"))
testthat::test_dir(here::here("tests", "testthat"))
rmarkdown::render(here::here("issues_for_field_teams.Rmd"))
rmarkdown::render(here::here("vegetation_report.Rmd"))
```
